title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). K is a field finitely generated over Q, with algebraic closure K̄. The notation is:
- E = E_{K̄/K} = Gal(K̄/K), the absolute Galois group.
- Γ is the Galois group of the constant field. In practice Γ is (an open subgroup of) Γ_Q = Gal(Q̄/Q).
- Π = Π_{K̄/K} = Gal(K̄/KQ̄), the 'geometric' part, i.e. the kernel of E → Γ.

The previous page states cd Π = n and cd_ℓ E = n+2 (ℓ odd), where n is the transcendence degree.

Theorem 1: every open subgroup E' of E has trivial centralizer in E; likewise for Π.

Proof strategy: a two-step dévissage along 1 → Π → E → Γ.

Step 1 (this page): the arithmetic part.
- Let Γ' be the (open) image of E' in Γ_Q. The image of the centralizer Z of E' centralizes Γ'. So it suffices to prove the Corollary: in Γ_Q the centralizer of every open subgroup is trivial.
- Proof of the Corollary. One may assume (OPS = 'on peut supposer') that Γ' is normal. Γ' = G_F for a number field F has trivial centre; this is flagged in the margin '? à vérifier'.
- Then Z ∩ Γ' ⊂ Z(Γ') = 1, so Z embeds in the finite group Γ_Q/Γ', hence Z is finite.
- By Artin–Schreier, the only nontrivial torsion elements of Γ_Q are the conjugates of complex conjugation τ.
- The centralizer of τ is {1, τ}, which is finite and so cannot contain the infinite group Γ'. Hence τ ∉ Z, and Z = 1.

Step 2 ('Revenons à'): the geometric part.
- Z has trivial image in Γ, so Z ⊂ Π.
- With Π' = E' ∩ Π (open in Π), one is reduced to Centr_Π(Π') = 1.
- The next page proves this for any profinite group that is a successive extension of free profinite groups. Π is such a group via a tower of curve fibrations of function fields; each step's geometric Galois group is free of infinite rank, by Douady.
- The argument uses the same dévissage (centralizer of an open subgroup maps into the centralizer of an open subgroup in the quotient), plus the facts that free profinite groups have trivial centre and are torsion-free.

What it serves (Scholie on the next page): trivial centre of E means the fundamental groupoid / Galois gerbe is determined up to unique isomorphism by the associated outer group. This is a basic rigidity input for the anabelian program of La Longue Marche.
errors: Not on this page, but in the dévissage it feeds: the corollary on the next page ('extension successive de groupes profinis libres') is false as stated if a free factor of rank 1 (Ẑ, abelian) is allowed. One needs free factors of rank ≥ 2, or of infinite rank as actually occurs for Gal(K̄/KQ̄).

'Il est bien connu que son centre est réduit à 1' (trivial centre of G_F for a number field F) is asserted without proof; Grothendieck himself marks it '? à vérifier'. It is true, e.g. via Hilbertianity or class field theory, but it is the crux of the argument.
Minor: 'centralisateur de τ dans Γ_{Q̄}' should read Γ_Q. The claim Centr(τ) = {1, τ} is correct, but it is used without justification.
Implicitly the image of E' in Γ is identified with an open subgroup of Γ_Q. This is fine only after replacing Γ by Gal(Q̄/Q ∩ K), which is open in Γ_Q.

ideas.what: Open subgroups of Gal(Q̄/Q) have trivial centralizer; proof via finiteness of the centralizer plus Artin–Schreier and self-centralizing complex conjugation
ideas.modern_name: Centralizers of open subgroups of absolute Galois groups of number fields are trivial
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard folklore (Neukirch school); see e.g. Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg, Cohomology of Number Fields, ch. XII
ideas.where_published: Implicit in the anabelian sections of Esquisse d'un programme / Letter to Faltings (centre-freeness); not stated as such

ideas.what: For K finitely generated over Q, open subgroups of G_K, and of its geometric part Gal(K̄/KQ̄), have trivial centralizers, by dévissage over the constant field
ideas.modern_name: Trivial centralizers of open subgroups for absolute Galois groups of finitely generated fields
ideas.usually_credited_to: Known in the anabelian literature (Pop, Nakamura, Fried–Jarden for Hilbertian fields)
ideas.where_published: Not explicitly; the theme appears in Letter to Faltings (1983)

ideas.what: Dévissage lemma: the 'trivial centralizers of open subgroups' property is stable under extensions, and holds for free profinite groups (of rank ≥ 2)
ideas.modern_name: Extension-stability of the 'slim' property (Mochizuki's terminology for profinite groups with trivial centralizers of open subgroups)

ideas.what: Trivial centre implies the Galois groupoid is determined up to unique isomorphism by its outer group (Scholie, next page)
ideas.modern_name: Centre-freeness / gerbes banded by outer groups; anabelian rigidity
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, Letter to Faltings); Giraud for the gerbe formalism
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme; Letter to Faltings

deep.surprise_reason: A clean early (c. 1981) proof sketch of what anabelian geometers later called 'slimness' of Galois groups of finitely generated fields. The facts and arguments are standard and appear in the later literature (Nakamura, Mochizuki, Pop), so this is mainly of historical interest as an early documented use of the dévissage.
transcription_corrections: 'Remarque :' is more likely 'Revenons à :' (returning to the proof of Theorem 1), followed by 'E' ⊂ E_{K̄/K}'.
The marginal note '? à vérifier' sits beside 'Il est bien connu que son centre est réduit à 1'.
'centralisateur de τ dans Γ_{Q̄}' is as written, but the sense is Γ_Q.
The sentence reads 'on veut donc voir que son centralisateur Z dans E_{K̄/K} a une image dans Γ réduite à {1}, donc Z ⊂ Π_{K̄/K}'.
